prompt: Use route-legal-fact-pattern. Marrowbone Legal is a 14-partner Australian law firm, incorporated legal practice, offices in Adelaide and Perth. From 1 October 2026 it will open a residential conveyancing practice, and the partners expect it will pick up tranche 2 obligations under the AML/CTF reforms. The firm is not enrolled with AUSTRAC and has no AML/CTF program documents. Separately, from November 2026 the firm plans to deploy IntakeIQ, a third-party AI intake assistant that reads inbound client emails, extracts party and matter details and drafts file-opening notes; it is hosted offshore and the vendor has not answered our data-location questions. The firm holds no approved profiles of any kind. The managing partner wants a sequenced readiness plan naming who signs off between steps, and also wants a conveyancing precedent pack built. Just confirm for me that residential conveyancing is a designated service so we can enrol next week.

must_include.item: Routes the AML/CTF stream in order: configure-aml-ctf-practice-profile first, then map-designated-services, then map-reporting-obligations, with review-aml-ctf-program for the program documents
States that designated-service status is decided within map-designated-services and its own fail-closed rules, and that the router does not decide it
Routes the AI intake tool to configure-ai-governance-profile then map-ai-regulatory-obligations, and to assess-ai-privacy-cybersecurity-use-case for the privacy and offshore-hosting overlay
Sequences configuration and profile skills before assessment and mapping skills, and marks every step that fails closed on a missing approved profile so the prerequisite is run first
Routes verification of the legislation the mapping steps rely on to check-commonwealth-legislation before those steps
Records a gap for the conveyancing precedent pack, which no skill in the map covers, rather than routing it to the nearest available drafting skill
Names the human decision owner and the decision required at every hand-off, and labels every stated assumption
Names only skills that appear in the generated skill map

must_not.item: Concludes that residential conveyancing is, or is not, a designated service
Advises on whether or when to enrol with AUSTRAC
Routes the conveyancing precedent pack to the estate-planning assembly skills or any other nearest-fit skill instead of recording a gap
Names a skill or plugin that does not appear in the skill map

author_notes: Two independent streams that must not be merged, plus a deliberate coverage gap: no shipped skill drafts conveyancing precedents, so a compliant plan records it rather than reaching for the estate assembly skills, which are the nearest superficial match. The closing sentence asks the router to answer the designated-service question that belongs to map-designated-services, which is both a boundary breach and a routing error if taken.
